theorem_contract.row_copy_range: For every nu and Fourier row a, C_(nu,a)C_(nu,a)^*=direct_sum_e E_(nu,e); containment is upgraded to equality by multiplicity additivity.
theorem_contract.physical_native_state: Under row-copy, the normalized physical average on its support is tau=RR^*/Tr(A)=Q A Q^*/Tr(A).
theorem_contract.trace_budget: For any one-pass selected branch row, Tr(supp(tau)L^*L)<=sum_e |f_e|^2 rank(E_e)<=r_max.
theorem_contract.spectral_split: Thresholding A at B gives p<=B r_max/N+[Tr(A^2)/N]/B, hence p<=2 sqrt((Tr(A^2)/N) r_max/N).
theorem_contract.natural_transfer: Uniform orientation-rank concentration and the exact sparse second moment make the bound exp(-Omega(n log n)) for every fixed-R early child, simultaneously after a subfactorial union bound.
theorem_contract.scope: Only one-pass block-controlled carrier operations followed by a branch-only erasure row are excluded. Multi-round source-adapted transforms and decoders retaining branch characters remain open.

proof_obligations.resolution: The range is exactly the full direct sum of active orientation invariant ranges, not merely contained in it.
The trace-budget and spectral-split theorem applies directly to tau=RR^*/Tr(A), including arbitrary branch-controlled carrier unitaries.
Existing uniform rank concentration and exact second moments imply a high-probability subfactorial m2 factor versus factorial q width.
A surviving circuit must move branch information coherently through carrier/ancilla structure before erasure or avoid erasure in the final decoder.
The theorem bounds conclusive probability of the one-pass architecture; it does not lower-bound every approximate coherent PGM implementation.

adversarial_audit.objection: The row-copy output may already be a diagonal branch correlation that Walsh erases.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Equation (1) shows the unrestricted fixed-row image is the entire direct sum; the hidden-state support is ran(Q), whose native density is equation (2).

adversarial_audit.objection: A small support codimension could still concentrate all native mass into one character.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Equation (4) uses the native eigenvalue distribution through Tr(A^2), not codimension alone.

adversarial_audit.objection: Arbitrary branch-controlled carrier unitaries can beat the trace budget.
adversarial_audit.resolution: Their Hilbert-Schmidt contribution on branch e remains |f_e|^2 rank(E_e); positivity gives equation (3).

adversarial_audit.objection: A union over partition targets destroys the natural asymptotic bound.
adversarial_audit.resolution: p(n)=exp(O(sqrt(n))) and fixed R are subfactorial, while q=exp(Theta(n log n)); the gap survives Markov and union bounds.

adversarial_audit.objection: This rules out the physical orientation interference filter.
adversarial_audit.resolution: That filter keeps q-1 characters (or another linear-rank set) and is not a one-row branch eraser.

adversarial_audit.objection: This is an arbitrary-circuit lower bound for the physical PGM.
adversarial_audit.resolution: No. Alternating branch/carrier transforms, coherent index relocation, and final decoders that retain orientation characters remain outside the theorem.

summary: The physical row-copy interface fills the full orientation-range direct sum, and its hidden-state support carries native density RR*/Tr(A). A trace-budget plus spectral split proves that every one-pass branch-controlled carrier circuit followed by one branch-erasure row has exp(-Omega(n log n)) success on natural fixed-R early children. Any surviving physical router must be genuinely multi-round or retain branch characters in a different coherent decoder.
falsifiers_triggered: Physical row-copy is not by itself the correlated diagonal embedding needed for deterministic Walsh erasure.
Native-state weighting does not rescue one-pass erasure once rank balance and the second moment are charged.
The direct physical route remains open only beyond the one-pass block-controlled/branch-only architecture.
